Key Activities: Manages a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.

Plans, develops and manages a comprehensive program of detailed analysis and evaluation across sectors and departments to improve existing data, develop new methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the application of divisional statistics.

Implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.

1. Decision making: Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.

Establishes strategic directions for the management of significant studies, proposes innovative solutions and recommends to senior officials of Statistics Canada new or modified statistical programs to address departmental goals and objectives.

Manages complex studies covering a range of departmental statistical programs, determines the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Plans and manages the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to certify the overall quality and completeness of program results, to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, to ensure the continued relevancy of data in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions and to extend the use of statistical programs

Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of divisional computer systems, equipment, databases and files. The data, systems and equipment are used by staff for the collection, compilation, distribution and analysis of a broad range of statistical and administrative information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination. Establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term program goals. Participates in the recruitment of staff and approves training and development plans. Allocates human and financial resource needs to achieve objectives. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff, reviews performance appraisals prepared by subordinate supervisors.

Evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of statistical systems and processes. Manages budgets including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the results of economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on complex policy issues, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data, on advanced analytical methods, concepts and techniques, and on economic and social science theories and principles.
Writes reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of statistical and analytical methods and approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.

Negotiates significant resources and services, timeframes and costs for large scale projects with service providers(e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic and sociological principles and theories, especially as they relate to a specialized area, and specific knowledge of the specialized area. This knowledge is required to provide expert advice on the results of surveys and studies to data users, to STC senior management and to other professionals within and outside STC.
Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Knowledge of management practices and the theories and principles of project management in order to manage staff, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of current and emerging socio-economic trends and issues in Canada and internationally such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to a broad area of expertise including all aspects of a statistical program.

Knowledge of STC policies, practices and classification systems as well as existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work, to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities, and to recommend changes.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Undertakes analytical studies evaluating the effectiveness of divisional statistical programs and the resulting products and services in order to determine the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources. Prepares reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

Identifies gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Conceptualizes enhancements and determines modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of the data in an area of specialty modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Researches and reports on trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations on the use and application of new computer hardware and software technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications; recommends strategies for the introduction or enhancement of statistical programs, the acquisition of new equipment and services and/or the adoption of new collection, production and dissemination strategies.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).
